cross_response_observations: The dominant failure category across responses A through G is some structural break in the upstream specification of either the move set, the play convention, the base case, or the dynamic-programming framework. Responses B and F break the move set in opposite directions (B drops 1, F adds non-power values), and although both produce wrong P/N strings the specific code differs. Responses A, B, and G all assert a wrong period for the P-positions: A claims period 2 (alternating P and N), B inherits a wrong period from its truncated move set, and G derives a wrong period from a misapplied Nim XOR framework. Responses E and G both misapply Sprague-Grundy-style frameworks: E computes Grundy values via mex of reachable values, while G applies the Nim XOR rule directly to a single pile. Responses D and E both truncate the output before 101 characters; for D the truncation co-occurs with a flipped base case, for E with the Grundy framework misapplication. Response C is the cleanest deviation: a consistent P/N convention swap that inverts every label without otherwise breaking the DP, producing a string that is the bitwise complement of the gold. Response H is pathological: it loops or truncates before committing to a final classification, so non_terminating_or_no_final_answer is its only applicable code. The single most common downstream code is arithmetic_recursion_error, present in six of the eight responses; it almost never appears as the load-bearing primary diagnostic because in each case some upstream error (move set, convention, base case, or framework) accounts for the wrong labels.
